source.locator: lines 15-24, motivating induction through successive arguments

findings.finding: After correctly describing every earlier step as computing h(x+1) from h(x), the source reverses the dependency in its concluding sentence and says h(x) is defined from h(x+1).
findings.controlling_evidence: The immediately preceding instances compute h(1) from h(0) and h(2) from h(1), and the recursive equation that follows likewise defines the successor value from the preceding value.
findings.required_translation_handling: State that h(x+1) is defined from h(x) and add an adjacent OLTECMPREC-001 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 20-27, computability explanation after the composition display

findings.finding: The source concludes the computation with h(x_0,...,x_{k-1}), although the displayed definition makes h an n-place function and reserves k for the number of inner functions and arguments of f.
findings.controlling_evidence: The displayed defining equation and the preceding sentence both give h the arguments x_0 through x_{n-1}; only the final occurrence substitutes k for n.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use h(x_0,...,x_{n-1}) in the computation and add an adjacent OLTECMPREC-002 disclosure.

findings.finding: The title says 'Primitive Recursion Functions', while the section definitions, propositions, and standard mathematical category throughout the body are primitive recursive functions.
findings.controlling_evidence: The opening review distinguishes primitive recursion as a construction from the functions closed under it, and lines 63-80 repeatedly name the resulting class 'primitive recursive functions.'
findings.required_translation_handling: Translate the title with the primitive-recursive-function meaning and add an adjacent OLTECMPREC-003 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 69-79, stage construction of the primitive recursive functions

findings.finding: The source defines S_{i+1} only from one construction applied to functions in S_i and omits S_i itself, so the stages need not be cumulative and later constructions cannot generally combine functions first appearing at different depths.
findings.controlling_evidence: The passage calls these stages a description of the smallest class closed under composition and primitive recursion. The equivalent stage construction must therefore retain each earlier stage while adding the one-step closure; otherwise its displayed union can omit mixed-depth compositions required by the preceding definition.
findings.required_translation_handling: Define S_{i+1} cumulatively by including every function in S_i as well as the one-step constructions, and add an adjacent OLTECMPREC-004 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 34-39, definition and naming of projection functions

findings.finding: Immediately after defining the n-place projections as Proj(n,i), the source calls them Proj(k,i), although k denotes the arity of the outer function in the surrounding composition construction.
findings.controlling_evidence: The displayed definition uses n for the projection's number of arguments, and the very next sentence again says Proj(n,i) is n-place. The isolated k is inconsistent with both.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use Proj(n,i) in the naming sentence and add an adjacent OLTECMPREC-005 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 13-23, construction of f(x)=2 times x

findings.finding: The source says the specific doubling function is obtained from const_n and multiplication, but the displayed composition on the next line correctly uses const_2.
findings.controlling_evidence: To obtain f(x)=2 times x, the constant supplied to multiplication must be 2; the immediately following equation explicitly supplies const_2.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use const_2 in the explanatory sentence and add an adjacent OLTECMPREC-006 disclosure.
